# Publish representative CPU performance and memory measurements

## Goal

Publish reproducible CPU measurements for the current release milestone. GPU
benchmarks and device crossover measurements are owned by #474.

## Maintainer GPU scope decision — 2026-11-13

GPU implementation and actual-device qualification are consolidated in #474,
separate from the current CPU release milestone. The maintainer has Apple Metal
hardware locally and no CUDA device or self-hosted NVIDIA runner. Metal and CUDA
require separate execution evidence; neither backend qualifies the other.
GPU requirements remain tracked and unqualified where evidence is missing, but
do not block this issue's CPU acceptance. Compile-only/fallback checks remain
useful and cannot count as device execution. See docs/DECISIONS.md item 17.

## Work

1. Use a fixed manifest of real/generated models for parsing, compilation, network
   generation, native finite solvers, NFcore/NFnext, CPU optional backends, scans and
   ensembles. Explicitly list missing CPU workload/backend coverage.
2. Record machine/OS/compiler/dependencies and source/build identity. Measure
   cold/warm startup, peak memory, allocations where measurable and throughput;
   include alternating A/A controls and preserve regressions/no-win experiments.
3. Run independent correctness checks alongside every measured workload. Report
   Apple-host CPU results and Linux CI results separately; do not generalize one
   machine's timings to all platforms or to Metal/CUDA.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `release-benchmarks`: reproducible machine/corpus/revision manifests cover all required CPU backends and workload classes. GPU measurements are tracked separately in #474.
- [ ] `release-benchmark-correctness`: every measured CPU workload passes canonical or analytic semantic checks.
- [ ] `release-obligation-174`: each CPU benchmark work clause has its named result, measurement limits, source/oracle identities and main commit recorded.

## Dependencies

#141, #148, CPU/ensemble work in #176. No GPU hardware prerequisite.

## Closing rule

Close when all acceptance criteria and work clauses for this issue's stated
scope pass on main with exact source/build identity and downstream artifacts.
No additional maintainer decision or closure approval is required.
title: G04: Publish representative CPU speed and memory baselines
